B"H
# Phase 2 — Gevurah Reality Gate

> Chesed dreams of worlds in flight; Gevurah measures every byte;
> the Awtsmoos gives the frame a bound, so living motion stays sound.

## Reality constraints
1. Do not rewrite unrelated site systems.
2. Do not invent a new rendering dependency until existing dependencies are traced.
3. Preserve each app's public route and identity unless evidence requires a migration.
4. Never partially patch a touched file; rewrite the complete touched file.
5. Split touched source files so executable logic remains below the project line-size law.
6. Use tab indentation and expanded readable functions.
7. Prefer shared contracts and adapters over copy/paste.
8. Validate AI-generated scene data before execution.
9. Keep timeline evaluation deterministic for testing.
10. Ensure mobile controls remain usable without hover.
11. Provide desktop affordances without making mobile a degraded afterthought.
12. Do not rely on screenshots alone for verification.
13. Check console errors and runtime state.
14. Test a long timeline, not only toy scenes.
15. Keep render backends swappable.
16. Separate scene data from renderer implementation.
17. Separate AI planning from execution.
18. Separate UI shell from playback engine.
19. Preserve backward compatibility where existing saved projects can be mapped safely.
20. Record every discovered app and whether it is migrated, adapted, or intentionally left alone.

## Expected implementation shape
A shared movie core should likely own schema validation, timeline evaluation, scene lifecycle, easing, animation primitives, character/shape/text semantics, procedural particles, camera intentions, and AI plan normalization. 2D and 3D backends should implement renderer-specific behavior. Each existing creator app should consume the shared core through a thin personality adapter and its own mobile-first shell/theme.

## Verification gate
No completion claim until the showcase movie demonstrates multiple scenes, people/characters, shapes, text, particles, infographic content, transitions, 2D/3D motion, changing angles/cameras where supported, and completes its ~180-second timeline without uncaught console errors.
